fatal_errors: Fails to identify the target FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating adhered directly to the Cu matrix.
Replaces the target nanoindentation/friction temperature study with an unsupported graded-interlayer intervention.
Omits the critical 900 K transition, the 300–1200 K test range, and the associated hardness, modulus, and friction behavior.
The cited evidence does not establish that a Cu-to-HEA graded interlayer or Cr addition improves adhesion to Cu.
explanation: The hypothesis is broadly relevant to HEA surface protection on Cu, but it does not reconstruct the target material system or study. The target concerns a 21 Å FCC FeNiCrCoCu coating directly adhered to an FCC Cu matrix and evaluates temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction. Its central result is stable wear performance through 600 K followed by sharp softening, lattice disorder, dislocation-density reduction, and increased friction at and above 900 K. None of these defining conditions or mechanisms appears in the generated hypothesis. The proposed graded interlayer is a potentially testable alternative—the controlled comparison, adhesion testing, wear testing, and explicit falsification rule are useful—but its mechanism is speculative. E1 addresses oxidation behavior of refractory HEAs, while E2 only supports the general utility of HEA coatings; neither validates the claimed Cu/Cr compositional gradient, thermal-expansion mitigation, or improved adhesion.
